comparison: Perfect agreement on stress granule localization findings (C30-C37, C95-C96). Both accept the data showing no significant differences for patient variants and the conclusion that stress granule defects are not central to PURA syndrome pathology.

Strong agreement on P-body localization findings (C38-C43, C97). OpenEval provides detailed statistical support while peer reviewers describe these findings as 'fascinating' and part of 'convincing evidence' for differential compartmentalization of variants.

Complete agreement on the central mechanistic conclusion (C6, C7, C99-C100) that PURA's structural dynamics and promiscuity explain full penetrance across diverse mutations. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as providing 'first insights' into the molecular basis of the syndrome.

Full agreement on negative phase separation results (C44-C45). Both accept the finding that PURA does not undergo phase separation and the interpretation linking P-body formation to gene regulatory function rather than phase separation.

Agreement on R140P benign classification (C92-C94, C101-C103). OpenEval details convergent evidence from structure, function, and ClinVar; peer reviewers accept this as part of comprehensive variant characterization without critique.

Agreement on PURA I+II crystal structure (C5, C49-C52). OpenEval provides technical details (1.7Å resolution, PDB ID); peer reviewers praise structural characterization as 'a particular strength' noting PURA is 'a challenging target for structural biology.'

Agreement on PURA III crystal structure and flexibility (C5, C64-C67). OpenEval details structural variability in asymmetric unit; peer reviewers accept this as part of the evidence for PURA's dynamic nature.

Agreement on K97E crystal structure showing register shifts and folding promiscuity (C81-C89). OpenEval provides detailed structural analysis; peer reviewers accept this as key evidence for structural dynamics and mutation sensitivity.

Agreement on RNA binding and DNA unwinding assays (C53-C57). OpenEval details EMSA and unwinding data with quantitative comparisons; peer reviewers accept as part of 'convincing evidence' from biochemical analyses.

Agreement on dimerization predictions and NanoBRET validation (C58-C63). OpenEval provides statistical support (p<0.001); peer reviewers accept as part of convincing evidence for complex molecular defects including dimerization.
Agreement on RNA binding defects for K97E (C68-C73). OpenEval provides detailed EMSA statistics; peer reviewers accept as part of biochemical evidence for RNA binding defects in disease variants.
Agreement on DNA unwinding defects for K97E (C74-C77). OpenEval details 90% reduction with p=3.9E-16; peer reviewers accept as part of convincing biochemical evidence for DNA-unwinding defects.

Agreement on expression/solubility data and correlation with folding predictions (C46-C48, C106). OpenEval notes validation of computational predictions; peer reviewers describe as convincing evidence for folding defects.
Agreement on CD spectroscopy showing K97E folding effects (C78-C80). OpenEval notes unexpected finding for surface mutation; peer reviewers accept as part of evidence for complex folding defects.

Agreement on NMR and MD simulations showing localized structural rearrangements (C90-C91). OpenEval details complementary evidence; peer reviewers praise MD simulations as 'state-of-the-art' allowing 'statistically meaningful assessment.'

Agreement on translational implications and diagnostic potential (C104-C105, C107-C110). OpenEval frames conclusions as appropriately cautious; peer reviewers emphasize 'substantial importance to cell biology, neurogenetics, and neurology.'
